name: TikTok
summary: Login Kit (TikTok's OAuth 2.0 login) is self-serve for your own account: you can register an app, add Login Kit, and test with a sandbox target user the same day. Opening it to any TikTok user requires submitting the app for TikTok review, which official docs put at several days to two weeks. If you also need to post content publicly, the separate Content Posting API audit decides the timeline, and TikTok does not publish its duration.

verdict.label: Moderate
verdict.timeToFirstConnection: Hours to about 1 day for your own account (sandbox target user, no review). Add a few hours if you need to set up URL verification first.
verdict.timeToProduction: About 1 to 3 weeks for Login Kit: 1 to 3 days of your own setup, plus the official review window of several days to two weeks. Add an unpublished, open-ended audit wait if you need public posting through the Content Posting API.
verdict.approvalWait: Official: review may take several days to two weeks after submission. Reported by a secondary source: Content Posting API audits of about 1 to 2 weeks for a clean submission. TikTok does not publish a duration for the Content Posting audit. Treat the secondary figure as unverified.
verdict.handsOnEffort: About 1 to 3 days for you: create the developer account and organization, register the app, configure Login Kit and redirect URIs, verify URLs, write the review explanation, and record a demo video. The agent can draft the config, policy text, and review script, and handle token code.

decideFirst.question: Do you need only sign-in and profile data (Login Kit), or do you also need to post videos (Content Posting API)?
decideFirst.guidance: Login Kit alone goes through the standard app review. Posting through the Content Posting API adds a separate audit. Until that audit passes, all content from your client is restricted to private viewing. Decide this first, because it changes the timeline more than anything else.

evidence.note: The official FAQ and the Photo endpoint page both state the private-viewing restriction for unaudited clients. Whether you need that path is your decision.

decideFirst.question: Will the app be registered under an organization or your personal developer account?
decideFirst.guidance: TikTok recommends an organization as the app owner and says personal registration is not recommended for real integrations. Create or join an organization before you register the app so ownership can transfer cleanly later.

decideFirst.question: Which scopes do you need? user.info.basic only, or additional user data and video scopes?
decideFirst.guidance: user.info.basic is added to every Login Kit app by default. Each additional scope must be requested and approved in your app's Scopes section, and approval alone does not give access to a user's data until that user authorizes it. Request the minimum set, because each extra scope is part of the review.

phases.name: 1 · Register the app and connect your own account
phases.goal: Get a client key and secret, enable Login Kit with a valid redirect URI, and complete an OAuth round trip with your own TikTok account.
phases.duration: Hours to 1 day (hands-on). No provider wait.

steps.title: Create a TikTok developer account
steps.detail: Sign up for a developer account with an email address. Accept the developer terms. The TikTok account you sign in with is separate from a consumer account.

steps.title: Create or join an organization (recommended)
steps.detail: Create an organization that will own the app. You will choose it as the owner when you register the app.

evidence.note: The official registration page recommends this step but does not require it. The organization guide URL was linked from the registration page; its contents were not read.

steps.title: Register the app in Manage apps
steps.detail: Sign in, open Manage apps, click Connect an app, and select the owning organization. Fill in the app details (name, icon, category, description, and the website URL for Web). Note the client key and client secret from the Credentials section.

evidence.note: The Manage apps link is on the official registration page.

steps.title: Add the Login Kit product and register redirect URIs
steps.detail: In the Products section, add Login Kit and register a redirect URI for each platform you use. Web URIs must be absolute https URLs with no query parameters or fragments, and you can register up to 10. The agent can write the callback handler and state check.

steps.title: Test with a sandbox and a target user
steps.detail: Switch to Sandbox mode, create a sandbox (up to 5 per app), and add your own TikTok account as a target user (up to 10 per sandbox). Authorize that account through Login Kit and run the authorization URL, code exchange, and a basic user info call. The agent can write and run this test.

evidence.note: The sandbox quota and target-user limit come from the official sandbox pages. One community guide says sandbox posts are limited to the owner's own account; that is consistent with sandbox scope, but it is not an official statement.

phases.name: 2 · Prepare the app for external users
phases.goal: Make the app's public pages and review package complete enough that TikTok can approve it on the first pass.
phases.duration: 1 to 3 days of hands-on work before you submit.

steps.title: Publish a Terms of Service page and a Privacy Policy
steps.detail: Publish both pages on your domain and enter their URLs in the app's basic information. The agent can draft the text, but you must review it and publish it under your legal authority.

evidence.note: Official requirement: for apps created after September 9, 2024, the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy URLs must be verified. Whether your policies are adequate is a legal decision for you.

steps.title: Verify URL properties
steps.detail: In Production mode, open URL properties and verify your domain (or a URL prefix by uploading a signature file). This is required for the Terms of Service URL, the Privacy Policy URL, and the Web URL. Any app that uses the Content Posting upload URL or Link Sharing must also verify those URLs.

evidence.note: Verification needs DNS or file-upload control of the domain, so a human with domain access must do it.

steps.title: Write the review explanation and record the demo video
steps.detail: In the App review section, explain how each product and scope is used in the app. Upload at least one demo video (up to 5 videos, 50 MB each) that shows the complete end-to-end login flow. The agent can draft the explanation and a click script. You record and upload the video.

evidence.note: Official review guidance states what must be explained and how many videos may be uploaded. The agent's draft content is not an official requirement.

steps.title: Submit for review
steps.detail: Click Save, then Submit for review. The app enters In review and cannot be edited until review ends. You can recall it to Draft if you need to change something.

phases.name: 3 · Provider review
phases.goal: TikTok reviews the app and either sets it to Live or returns review comments.
phases.duration: Official: several days to two weeks after submission. Reported: longer for the Content Posting audit, which TikTok does not time publicly.

steps.title: Wait for review and monitor status
steps.detail: Track the status under Production: Draft, In review, Live, or Not approved. Until the app is Live, the APIs are not usable.

evidence.note: The official review timeline is several days to two weeks. A community source tied to a different TikTok product reports a 3 to 4 week window, which is not an official figure for Login Kit.

steps.title: Respond to review comments and resubmit
steps.detail: If the app is not approved, open the History icon for the review comments, fix each item, and resubmit. The agent can make the code and copy changes. You must submit them.

steps.title: Request the Content Posting API audit (only if you post publicly)
steps.detail: Apply for the audit that lifts the private-viewing restriction. TikTok does not publish a duration for it. Community guides report about 1 to 2 weeks for clean submissions, but that figure is not official.

evidence.note: The official pages require the audit but do not give a timeline. Secondary guides disagree on the duration, so use a longer buffer for planning.

phases.name: 4 · Ship and keep it running
phases.goal: Serve real users reliably: refresh tokens in the background, handle revocation, and plan for user caps.
phases.duration: Agent build work of about 1 to 3 days, plus monitoring after launch.

steps.title: Build a server-side token refresh job
steps.detail: Store the access token, refresh token, open_id, scope, and expiry times for each user. Refresh the access token a little before it expires, and replace the stored refresh token each time you refresh. If the refresh fails with invalid_grant, send the user through login again.

evidence.note: The token lifetimes and rotation behavior are on the official user token page, and the refresh timing advice is on the official silent-login page. A secondary source reports a different access token lifetime; see nuances.

steps.title: Add user revocation
steps.detail: Call the revoke endpoint when a user disconnects your app. The user will then no longer see the app under Manage app permissions.

steps.title: Plan for the active user cap
steps.detail: New apps start with an active user cap. You can request an increase through the official support form, but only after the app is in production, and not every request is granted.

requirements.note: Created by you with an email address.
Recommended by TikTok, not mandatory. Personal ownership is discouraged for real integrations.

requirements.item: Login Kit product with a valid redirect URI
requirements.requiredFor: Any OAuth login for web, iOS, Android, or desktop
requirements.note: Web URIs must be https, static, absolute, under 512 characters, and free of fragments. Up to 10 per app.

requirements.item: Terms of Service URL and Privacy Policy URL, verified
requirements.requiredFor: Submitting any app created after September 9, 2024
requirements.note: The verification needs domain or file-upload control.

requirements.item: Demo video showing the full flow
requirements.note: At least one video, up to 5, each up to 50 MB.

requirements.item: App icon (1024 x 1024, JPEG or PNG, up to 5 MB)

requirements.requiredFor: Any data or action beyond the default user.info.basic scope
requirements.note: Requested per scope in the Scopes section, then reviewed.

requirements.item: Content Posting API product and audit
requirements.requiredFor: Publishing public content for users through the API
requirements.note: Until the audit passes, posts are restricted to private viewing.

scopeTiers.consequence: Added to all Login Kit apps by default. It returns only a limited set of profile fields: open_id, union_id, avatar fields, and display_name.

scopeTiers.tier: Additional user info and video scopes
scopeTiers.examples: Scopes beyond the default, requested in the app's Scopes section
scopeTiers.consequence: Each requested scope must be approved in review. Users must also grant each scope when they authorize.

evidence.note: The specific scope names beyond user.info.basic were not read on the reference page, so no scope names are listed here.

scopeTiers.examples: Content Posting API direct post and upload
scopeTiers.consequence: Unaudited clients can post only to private accounts, as SELF_ONLY, and the attempt is blocked otherwise.

evidence.note: The per-day cap of 5 users for unaudited clients is from secondary sources only and is not verified against an official page.

scopeTiers.examples: Data request products on a user's behalf
scopeTiers.consequence: Requires a separate application with its own official timeline of about 3 to 4 weeks, plus Login Kit approval. Approval of one does not enable the other.

blockers.symptom: invalid_request: Redirect_uri is not matched with the uri when requesting code.
blockers.cause: The redirect URI in the authorization request, the token request, or the registered Login Kit settings differs.
blockers.fix: Use the exact registered URI in both steps, with no extra parameters or fragments, and make sure the Web URI is https.

blockers.symptom: The callback returns an error parameter saying the user is not eligible for third-party login.
blockers.cause: The user is not eligible, or the app is not yet approved for the requested use.
blockers.fix: Handle the error on the callback, show a clear message, and check the app status under Production.

evidence.note: The eligibility wording is from the official Login Kit web guide. The approval cause is an inference.

blockers.cause: The client has not passed the Content Posting API audit, and the creator account is public.
blockers.fix: Test with a private account and send SELF_ONLY for testing. For public posting, pass the audit.

evidence.note: The error code and the private-account rule are on the official Photo endpoint page. The second-hand guidance on test accounts is secondary.

blockers.cause: The refresh token is expired, has been revoked, or is an older token that was replaced by a rotated one.
blockers.fix: Store the newest refresh token from each response and send the user through login again.

blockers.symptom: Approved for data portability, but the API still returns no access.
blockers.cause: Login Kit approval is separate from the Data Portability application, and both must be approved.
blockers.fix: Check the app page for both. If both are approved and access still fails, contact support with Data Portability API as the topic.

nuances.title: Token lifetimes and rotation
nuances.detail: The official user token page states that the access token is valid for 24 hours and the refresh token for 365 days. The refresh response can return a new refresh token, and the old one must not be reused. A secondary guide reports a 24-hour and 365-day lifetime as well, and an older snippet from the same official page listed 2 hours and 180 days. The current page text is the more recent source.

evidence.note: Conflict recorded. The fetched official page (last updated August 4, 2026) is the basis for this guide.

nuances.title: Per-user authorization, not per-app
nuances.detail: Each TikTok user authorizes your app separately and gets their own tokens keyed by open_id. Approval of a scope does not grant access to anyone's data until that user consents.

nuances.title: Redirect URI rules
nuances.detail: Web redirect URIs must be absolute https, static (no query parameters), without a fragment, and under 512 characters. Up to 10 can be registered. Android redirects must be App Links or Deep Links, and iOS redirects must be Universal Links with the Associated Domains capability.

nuances.title: Unreleased apps are reviewed at TikTok's discretion
nuances.detail: TikTok says beta, incomplete, or test apps are generally not approved for integration. For a new app with no launch yet, TikTok may require an integration assessment with reasoning and UX mockups, and may approve or reject at its discretion.

evidence.note: This applies to apps that have not launched. It is the most likely reason a pre-launch app is rejected. The assessment is an official route, but its timeline is not published.

nuances.title: Policy on posting content
nuances.detail: Until the Content Posting API audit passes, every post from your client is restricted to private viewing. A secondary guide says TikTok's content sharing rules do not allow utility tools that only upload to accounts the operator manages. If your agent is a posting tool for other people's accounts, check this with TikTok before you build it.

evidence.note: The utility-tool rule comes from a secondary source that quotes TikTok's content sharing guidelines. It was not checked against the official guidelines.
